Application Materials.content:
- Supporting documents usually include: evidence of qualifications (**certificates or transcripts**); evidence of English language ability, if English is not your first language; a research proposal (check the department website for instructions, as these vary); and any additional department requirements (for example, some courses ask for specific information in a personal statement).
- You may need **two references**; referees will be contacted and asked to submit a reference directly via the referee portal.
- If you cannot upload supporting documents, there is often a field to explain why so you can still submit your application; instructions are then given on how to add documents via an online portal.
- If any certificates or transcripts are not in English, you should include **official, authenticated English translations**. The translation should be on official letter-headed paper, state that it is an accurate translation of the original, and include: the translator or translation company's name and contact details; credentials or qualifications; the date of translation; and the translator's full name and signature, or the full name and signature of an authorised official from the translation company.
- The translation should be done by an official translator/translation service. Translations by agents are not accepted unless the agency offers a recognised translation service and the translator can demonstrate appropriate credentials.

Interview Requirements.content:
- You **may be invited to attend an interview** as part of the application process for your chosen course.
- If so, you will receive further information, including the **date and time**, by email.
- You can check the application and selection information on the course profile page to see if an interview will be required for your course.

Application Deadlines.content:
- **Year of entry: 2026**; the academic year begins **September 2026**.
- **Applications for 2026 entry** are handled through a **staged admissions process** with selection deadlines throughout the year.
- **Stage 1:** Application received by **7th December 2025**; application update by **20th February 2026**.
- **Stage 2:** Application received by **1st March 2026**; application update by **1st May 2026**.
- **Stage 3:** Application received by **3rd May 2026**; application update by **19th June 2026**.
- **Stage 4:** Application received by **5th July 2026**; application update by **31st July 2026**.
- Applications received after the final selection deadline will be considered at the university's discretion if places are still available.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **High 2:1 honours degree (or overseas equivalent).**
- In your application, you should demonstrate aptitude, knowledge and/or interest in three areas: data analytics and/or statistics; computational subjects; and pathway specific requirements. These can be demonstrated by course units taken at undergraduate level and high school level, or professional experience.
- For this pathway, applicants are expected to evidence an interest and/or experience in topics related to environmental analysis. Examples include working experience in environment-themed topics (e.g. environment, climate, natural ecosystems, human social and economic systems, and health); experience in data science, GIS or environmental based data analysis; and evidence of training in environment-themed methods or topics.
- The course welcomes applicants from a range of STEM, business and humanities backgrounds.
- Due to competition for places, preference is given to students from high ranking institutions and with grades above the minimum entry requirements.
- For applicants from China (Mainland): taught master's applicants with a bachelor's degree from a recognised good-quality Chinese university, with a minimum overall average grade of **80%** or a minimum **GPA of 3.0 (out of 4.0)**, will be considered for admission to taught master's programmes; individual programme requirements also apply.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Applicants whose first language is not English should meet the following language requirements:
- **IELTS Academic: 7.0 overall with no component score below 6.5**.
- **TOEFL iBT: 100 with no score below 22 in each section**. TOEFL code for Manchester is **0757**.
- **Pre-Sessional English Courses:** applicants who do not meet these scores may be required to complete a pre-sessional English language course at the University of Manchester prior to the start of the course.
- For this programme, the minimum IELTS (Academic) scores for pre-sessional consideration are:
- **6 Week Pre-Sessional Course:** **IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each sub-skill**.
- **10 Week Pre-sessional Course:** **IELTS 6.0 overall with 6.0 in three sub-skills, and 5.5 in no more than one sub-skill**.
- If you have not yet completed your current academic study and are interested in studying a pre-sessional course, you must hold an **IELTS for UKVI (Academic)** test certificate to ensure that you are eligible for a separate visa for the English language course.
- Some English Language test results are only valid for **two years**. Your English Language test report must be valid on the **start date of the course**.
- Applicants from [majority English-speaking countries](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/admissions/language-requirements/) (or applicants who have studied for a full bachelor's degree or higher from one of these countries) may be exempt from submitting further evidence of English language proficiency.
- The University also provides [country-specific information](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/country-specific-information/) on the academic and English language qualifications which may be accepted from your country.

Program Overview.content:
- **Duration:** **1 year**. **Degree awarded:** **MSc**. **Study mode:** **Full-time: In person**.
- This MSc Data Science (Earth and Environmental Analytics) prepares students for a career in data science, with a focus on data techniques and uses most relevant to environmental management. It applies data-driven insights to current environmental challenges such as Climate Change, Biodiversity and Conservation, Natural Hazards, and Environment and Health.
- The course develops skills in data analysis, project design, computational methods, and data stewardship. It is intended for graduates from a broad range of disciplines, and welcomes applicants from STEM, business and humanities backgrounds to create a diverse cohort.
- The course aims to help students understand and respond to the complex interactions between the environment, climate, natural ecosystems, human social and economic systems, and health; ask important research questions; evaluate evidence; select appropriate methods; visualise, interpret and provide strategic advice and insight; and develop into agile data scientists able to work in interdisciplinary settings.
- Special features include an **interdisciplinary approach** and **hands-on** experience analysing real-world data using software such as **R, Python, and Excel**. The course is taught by an interdisciplinary team through lectures, computer based practicals, e-learning, meetings with industry partners, workshops, group work, and individual research.
- A master’s degree is formed of **180 credits**. **120 credits** are made up of a mix of mandatory and optional course units, and the remaining **60 credits** are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of a **12,000-to-15,000-word dissertation**. Dissertation research is supported by weekly research methodology lectures designed to improve academic, research and writing skills.
- Graduates develop a highly valued skillset that enhances employability across sectors such as policy, business, research and more. Previous students have gone on to roles such as **data scientists, civil servants, consultants, researchers, entrepreneurs, and in AI**. The University states that this MSc provides data skills for careers in banking and financial services, the Civil Service, the IT and tech sector, high performance sports analysis, large retail chains, and the pharmaceutical industry. Students also have access to the University’s dedicated [Careers Service](https://www.careers.manchester.ac.uk/) during the course and for two years after graduation.
- The course is offered at a university ranked top 10 in the UK for maths, statistics and computer science (Times Higher Education World University Rankings by Subject, 2025), and the University of Manchester is described as one of the UK’s most targeted universities by top employers (High Fliers, The Graduate Market Report 2024).

Curriculum.content:
- **Duration:** **1 year**.
- **Delivery format:** **Full-time: In person**.
- A master’s degree is formed of **180 credits**. **120** of these credits are made up by a mix of mandatory and optional course units, worth **15 credits each**. You will need to select **eight** of these course units, with **60 credits taken each semester**.
- The core units are:
- Statistics and Machine Learning 1: Statistical Foundations (**DATA70121**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- Statistics & Machine Learning 2: AI, Complex Data, Computationally Intensive Statistics (**DATA70132**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- Understanding Databases (**DATA70141**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- Applying Data Science (**DATA70202**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- Understanding Data and their Environment (**DATA71011**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- The remaining **60 credits** are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of a **12,000-to-15,000-word dissertation**. Your dissertation must be within the area of one of the course units you have chosen.
- Optional course units range from statistical foundations to environmental based data analysis and GIS. Examples shown on the page include:
- Privacy, Confidentiality and Disclosure Control (**DATA70402**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Measuring and Predicting 2 (**EART60071**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Computational Subsurface Geoscience (**EART60152**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Key Interpretation Skills (**EART60381**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Earth and Environmental Data Science (**EART60702**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Environmental Monitoring and Modelling (**EART62012**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Pollutant Mobility and Transformation (**EART62022**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Pollution Management in Practice 2 (**EART63012**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Environmental Remote Sensing (**GEOG60941**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Understanding GIS (**GEOG71551**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Neighbourhood Planning Project (**PLAN60812**, 15 credits, Optional)
- The page notes: "Displaying 10 of 17 course units" and provides [Display all course units](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/courses/list/18096/msc-data-science-earth-and-environmental-analytics/#).

Estimated accommodation costs for postgraduate students:
- The University of Manchester halls of residence (**catered**): **£555-£982 per month**.
- The University of Manchester halls of residence (**self-catered**): **£487-£1,060 per month**; some studio flats available for master's students up to **£1,255 per month**.
- Room in private halls (with average bills cost included): **£860-£1,010 per month**.
- Privately rented house shares (with average bills cost included): **£645-£710 per month**.
- The University of Manchester self-catered accommodation can range from **£4,853 to £12,096 a year**. [Read more information on accommodation costs at The University of Manchester](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/accommodation/student-accommodation/).

Financial Aid.content:
[MSc Data Science (Earth and Environmental Analytics)](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/courses/list/18096/msc-data-science-environmental-analytics/) is included in the full list of courses where Equity and Merit Scholarships are available for international master's students.
- There are **30 scholarships** available: **20 for full-time, on-campus master’s** study and **10 for part-time, distance learning master’s** study.
- The scholarships **cover full tuition fees** and, for students studying in Manchester, also include **return international airfares, living expenses and visas**.
- The scheme is open to applicants from **Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda and Zimbabwe**.
- To apply, applicants need to be a resident citizen of one of those countries, have **at least two years of professional experience** related to their chosen field of study, hold a bachelor’s degree with an overall excellent grade (typically **top 10% of your class**), and show commitment to returning home and making a positive impact.
- Applicants who met the eligibility requirements for the Equity and Merit Scholarship programme were invited to make an academic application for their chosen master’s course, and **an offer of admission is required** before the scholarship application can be shortlisted.
- For **September 2026 entry**, applications closed on **31 August 2025**. The timeline for 2026/27 was: **1 to 31 August 2025** scholarship application window, **September 2025** eligibility checks, **1 to 31 October 2025** academic application window, **November 2025 to May 2026** review period, **June 2026** results announced, and **September 2026** start of the academic year.
- More information: [Equity and Merit programme](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/about/social-responsibility/social-inclusion/equity-merit/)

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
- If your School or Department Admissions Team agrees to your request to defer, you may do so **without paying a deposit**.
- If you’ve already paid the deposit and then decide to defer, your payment will be carried over and used towards your tuition fees for the new entry year.
- If the CAS deposit increases for your new entry year, you’ll need to pay the difference before your new CAS can be issued.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Applicants who do not meet the English language scores for this programme may still be considered, but **may be required to complete a pre-sessional English language course at the University of Manchester prior to the start of the course**.
- **6 Week Pre-Sessional Course**: IELTS **6.5 overall** with **6.0 in each sub-skill**.
- **10 Week Pre-sessional Course**: IELTS **6.0 overall** with **6.0 in three sub-skills**, and **5.5 in no more than one sub-skill**.
- If you have not yet completed your current academic study and are interested in studying a pre-sessional course, you **must hold an IELTS for UKVI (Academic) test certificate** to ensure that you are eligible for a separate visa for the English language course.
